title: Tenant eviction triggered after KV-cache memory growth leads to reserved-capacity shortfall
creator: Aisha Reynolds
description: High-severity customer escalations (2 enterprise tenants) after a multi-hour traffic pattern caused large in-memory KV-cache growth on a subset of nodes. The autoscaler / allocator interpreted increased node-level memory reservations as reclaimed headroom and triggered tenant evictions from warm reserved slots, which in turn forced many requests to fallback cold pools and caused sustained capacity shortfalls for other tenants. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, and the long-term code and telemetry changes needed to prevent similar reserved-capacity misreconciliation in the future.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create two large tenants with persistent long-context workloads that populate KV cache heavily.
2) Constrain remaining cluster headroom by limiting spare GPUs in the test reserved pool.
3) Simulate a 2–3 hour steady traffic ramp with frequent token streaming to force KV cache growth.
4) Observe allocator metrics: memory-reserved vs headroom-reported and autoscaler evictions when eviction_thresholds are reached.
5) Validate tenant evictions correlate with step-down events and depleted burst credits for several tenants.
impact_summary: Customer impact: two enterprise customers experienced repeated cold-fallbacks and increased latency (p50 up 3x, p95 spiking to 12s) and token-cost increases due to fallbacks. Platform impact: reserved-pool availability dropped by ~28% for 45 minutes during the incident window, triggering additional customer escalations and a Priority support case.
investigation_summary: Initial triage (03-10): observed node memory reservation metrics rising without corresponding scheduler allocations. Heap profiling of runtime showed KV-cache per-tenant entries retained across requests; cache draining logic did not account for long-context sticky streams. Allocator logic (lease accounting) reads node.available_memory which is computed after accounting for soft-reserved kv-cache budget; however, a recent refactor (runtime-1.19) inverted a predicate causing the autoscaler to treat growing cache reservations as newly freed memory in its headroom delta calculation. This led to premature eviction decisions when combined with conservative burst-credit accounting for small tenants.
temporary_mitigation:
1) Immediately disabled the aggressive eviction path for reserved pools via feature flag: autoscaler.eviction.force_disable=true (applied 03-11 02:10 UTC).
2) Increased reserved-pool buffer for affected AZ by +20% to avoid further cascading evictions.
3) Contacted affected customers with explanation and ETA for a fix; granted a one-week credit and enabled higher-priority routing to reduce cold fallbacks.
code_changes: Planned patch: (a) revert inverted predicate introduced in runtime-1.19 that misclassifies kv-cache reservations in headroom delta; (b) add explicit kv-cache soft-limit gating so autoscaler accounts for sticky cache memory separately from schedulable headroom; (c) add unit tests for headroom delta under varied cache growth scenarios; (d) extend integration test harness to simulate sustained long-context streams and validate no eviction occurs when only KV-cache grows.
rollout_plan:
1) Land small revert and unit tests to canary branch (canary-az) and run overnight soak (03-16).
2) If canary stable for 6 hours under synthetic load, rollout to Dedicated control-plane with staged AZ rollout (03-17).
3) Monitor consumer-facing dashboards and alert if reserved-pool free capacity falls below 10% within 30m after rollout.
4) Disable temporary mitigation flags after 24 hours of stable telemetry.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for headroom delta arithmetic covering negative, zero, and positive kv-cache deltas.
- Integration test with dedicated-reserved-pool emulator and synthetic long-context generator.
- Chaos test: force GC delay and validate autoscaler does not evict correctly-warmed tenants.
- Prepost validation: run the production in-region canary traffic replay for 2 hours and compare p95/p99 latencies to baseline.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Add targeted metrics and alerts:
- autoscaler.kvcache_reservation_bytes (per-node, per-az)
- autoscaler.headroom_delta_inspected (histogram)
- allocator.eviction_reason{kvcache_misaccount}=true count
Create alert: reserved_pool.available_ratio < 0.12 for > 10m with autoscaler.eviction_count > 0 => P0 paging to SRE and on-call infra.
customer_communication: Drafted message for affected tenants explaining root cause, immediate mitigations, and timeline for fix. Support lead (Jamal Ortiz) to schedule 30m follow-ups with each customer on 03-16. Communication includes runbook links, incident dashboard, and rollback plan.
notes: PM review requested 03-12: increase priority for tenants flagged as enterprise-tier.
Design input (cache team) recommends separate metric namespace for sticky cache vs ephemeral allocations.
SRE recommends holding canary for 24h if synthetic load indicates any eviction events.
